title: Normalize observed Unicode citation markers without weakening provenance
description: The real 7B medium-effort app chat returned a correct paper answer with a known chunk ID wrapped as 【source:UUID】. The ASCII-only validator rejected it with UNGROUNDED_OUTPUT. Normalize this observed formatter variation before validation and final persistence; preserve strict supplied-document evidence checks.
acceptance_criteria: Given valid supplied evidence in the observed Unicode citation wrapper, when a chat or summary completes, then its content uses canonical [source:UUID] markers and its source/page citations persist.
Given unknown, malformed or foreign-document evidence, when its wrapper is normalized, then it cannot become a valid citation, including mixed valid and invalid markers.
Given streamed Unicode markers, when the final event arrives, then canonical persisted content replaces the partial stream and citation navigation works after refresh.
Existing failed generations remain failed; normalization does not replay model requests or fabricate source IDs.
test_cases: Unit tests for canonical/Unicode/mixed wrappers and malformed/foreign IDs.
Isolated real PostgreSQL chat SSE/final persistence and summary/checkpoint tests.
Real retained 7B medium chat with page references; fixture browser regression.
verification: Unit RED: 12 failed/6 passed; real DB RED: 13 failed/1 passed; resumed-cache RED: four failed. Final full backend 279 passed in 39.54s; independent 36 citation targets passed. Browser fixture emits Unicode medium markers; deletion/default and low-summary/medium-chat scenarios passed in 48.7s. Real retained 7B low summary completed in 44.39s, medium chat in 14.73s with 54 SSE events and canonical page citations. Strict document/chunk membership, checkpoint configuration, zero hosted reservations and original failed-message preservation verified in PostgreSQL. All persisted outputs/defaults/controls and original PDF survived six-service restart.
